meditation.text: Hello, and welcome, {name}.
Let's set this time aside, just for you.
Find a posture that feels steady and easy, and let the eyes close, or soften toward the floor.
There is nothing to achieve here. Nothing to fix. You can let all of that go for now.
Take one deeper breath, in through the nose, and let it out slowly.
And let the breathing return to its own natural rhythm.
Begin to notice where you feel the breath most clearly. Perhaps the belly, rising and falling. Perhaps the cool air at the tip of the nose.
You do not need to control it. Just feel it, one breath at a time.
The in-breath, arriving.
And the out-breath, leaving.
Feel the weight of the body, settled and supported, held by the floor or the chair.
Before long, the mind will wander, into a thought, a plan, a memory. This is completely normal.
The moment you notice you have drifted, that is the practice working, not failing.
Gently, and without any judgment, guide your attention back to the breath.
Again, the breath in.
And a slow breath out.
There is nowhere else you need to be. Just here, with this breath, and then the next.
Rest in the simple rhythm of it.
Let the breath breathe itself, and let the quiet grow wide around you.
Each return, gentle. Each breath, enough, {name}.
In a moment, we will finish.
Let your attention widen to the room around you, the sounds, the light.
And when you feel ready, {name}, let your eyes open, carrying a little of this stillness with you.
Welcome back, {name}. Let's begin.
Settle into a position you can hold with ease, and allow your eyes to close.
Let the body arrive first. Feel the places where it touches the seat, the floor, your hands resting.
Take a slow breath in, and a longer breath out, letting the shoulders drop.
Now, simply listen. Notice the sounds around you, near and far, without naming them or following them.
Let the sounds come and go on their own. You do not have to do anything with them.
And now bring your attention to the body as a whole, sitting here, breathing.
Notice any sensation that stands out. Warmth, coolness, a tingling, a place of holding. Meet it with a little curiosity.
There is no need to change anything. Only to notice, and to allow.
When a thought pulls you away, and it will, softly note it, thinking, and return to the body.
Come back to the breath, and the simple feeling of sitting here.
Breathing in, aware of the whole body.
Breathing out, letting it soften.
Rest in this open awareness, letting whatever arises simply pass through.
Nothing to chase. Nothing to hold. Just this present moment, {name}, unfolding.
Steady, and still.
In a moment, we will close.
Wiggle the fingers, and let the breath deepen a little.
And whenever you are ready, {name}, open your eyes.

sleep.text: Rest easy, {name}.
The day is done. There is nothing more you need to do tonight.
Let yourself be fully supported by the bed, and let it take your weight.
Breathe in slowly, and let the out-breath be long, and soft.
Let your attention move gently to the top of your head, and let it soften.
Soften the forehead. Let the space between the eyebrows smooth out.
Let the eyes grow heavy. Unclench the jaw, and let the tongue rest.
Let the neck and the throat release.
Feel the shoulders drop away from the ears, growing heavy.
Let that heaviness spread down the arms, to the elbows, the wrists, the hands.
Let the chest and the belly rise and fall on their own.
Let the hips settle, and the legs grow heavy, all the way down to the feet.
There is nothing to hold now. Nothing to carry.
With each breath out, sink a little deeper into the bed.
If a thought appears, let it float by, like a cloud you do not need to follow.
You do not need to stay awake for me. It is alright to drift.
Let everything grow soft, and slow, and quiet.
You are safe, and warm, and held, {name}.
Rest now.
It's time to rest, {name}.
Let the day settle behind you. You can set it all down now.
Find the position that feels most comfortable, and let your eyes close.
Take one slow breath in, and sigh it out.
Feel your body growing heavier with each breath, sinking into the bed.
We will drift down slowly, like descending a soft, quiet stair, one gentle step at a time.
With the next breath out, let go of the shoulders.
The next, let go of the arms, and the hands.
The next, let the back and the belly soften.
And the next, let the legs grow heavy, and still.
Nothing to do now but breathe, and sink, and rest.
Each breath, a little slower. Each moment, a little quieter.
Let the thoughts of the day dissolve, one by one, into the dark.
There is nowhere to be. Nothing to solve. Only rest.
Let sleep come to you in its own time, all on its own.
Sleep well, {name}.

flow.text: Alright, {name}. Let's get you ready.
Sit tall, both feet on the floor, and let the shoulders settle down the back.
Take a slow breath in, and let it go completely.
Notice the swirl of the day, all the tabs open in your mind.
Picture that clutter as sediment, stirred up in a glass of water.
You do not have to push it away. Just stop stirring, and let it begin to settle.
With each breath out, the water grows a little clearer.
Take one more slow, deliberate breath.
And as the water clears, a single thing comes into focus.
Bring to mind the one thing you are here to do.
Hold it simply, without pressure. A clear, quiet intention.
Let your attention gather around it, like light drawn to a single point.
Calm, and alert. Relaxed, and sharp.
This is the state you work from, {name}. Settled, and clear, and ready.
Take one last easy breath.
And when you are ready, {name}, open your eyes, and begin.
Let's find your focus, {name}.
Sit up, tall and easy, and feel the length of the spine.
Take a breath that fills you a little more than usual, and let it out slowly.
Roll the shoulders back once, and let them settle.
Feel yourself becoming present, right here, in this seat, at this moment.
Let the worries of earlier, and the plans for later, rest at the edges for now.
Bring your attention to a single point, the feeling of the breath at the nose.
Rest your focus there, light and steady, like a hand on a still surface.
When it drifts, and it will, simply bring it back, without any fuss.
This is training. Each return sharpens the mind a little more.
Now, name for yourself the one task in front of you.
See yourself moving into it, {name}, calm, and capable, and clear.
The mind is quiet. The path is simple. One thing, done well.
Take a full breath in, and let it wake you up a little.
And when you are ready, {name}, open your eyes, and step into the work.

relax.text: Welcome, {name}. Let's take a little time to unwind.
Settle into your seat, and let yourself fully arrive.
Let your eyes close, or rest softly, wherever they land.
Breathing in, silently say to yourself, I settle.
Breathing out, I ease.
Again. Breathing in, I settle.
Breathing out, I ease.
Let the jaw unclench, and the shoulders drop away from the ears.
Let your hands rest open, and heavy.
There is nothing to chase right now. Nowhere you have to be.
This moment, just as it is, is enough.
Feel the breath moving through you, slow and easy, like a gentle tide.
With each breath out, let a little more of the day loosen, and fall away.
Warm, and unhurried. Held, and at ease.
Let the whole body soften, and rest, like something set down at last.
Stay here, in this ease, as long as you like, {name}.
And when you are ready, carry a little of this calm with you.
Take a breath, {name}. Let's set the day down.
Find a comfortable place to be, and let the body relax into it.
Take a slow breath in through the nose, and let it out through the mouth, with a soft sigh.
Bring to mind, gently, anything you have been carrying today.
You do not have to solve it now. Just notice it, and loosen your grip a little.
Squeeze your shoulders up toward your ears, hold, and then let them drop.
Feel the difference between holding on, and letting go.
Let that letting-go spread through the arms, the chest, the belly.
Soften the muscles of the face, and the space behind the eyes.
Breathe in ease. Breathe out tension.
There is nothing to hurry toward. This time is yours.
Let yourself be exactly as you are, with nothing to fix, and no one to be.
Sink into the quiet comfort of simply resting here.
Let the breath be slow, and the body be soft.
When you are ready, {name}, return gently, a little lighter than before.

stress-relief.text: It's okay, {name}. Let's steady this, together.
Feel your feet on the floor, and the seat beneath you, holding you up.
You are here. Right now, in this moment, you are safe enough.
Let's lengthen the breath. Breathe in slowly, through the nose.
And breathe out, even more slowly, letting it be long.
Again. In, slow and steady.
And out, long, and complete.
Notice a few things you can hear, near, and far away.
Whatever you are feeling right now, you do not have to push it away.
Let it be here, without fighting it. Feelings move through, like weather across the sky.
This feeling is real, and it is temporary. It will pass, as it always has.
Meet it the way you would meet a friend in pain, with a little kindness.
Steadier now. Keep the breath long, and slow.
Let the ground hold you. You do not have to hold yourself up alone.
You have moved through hard moments before, {name}. You can move through this one too.
One more slow breath, in.
And out.
Let's take this one breath at a time, {name}.
Plant your feet, and feel the solid ground underneath them.
Let your breath slow down. Breathe in, for a count of four.
Hold, gently, for a moment.
And out, for a count of six, longer than the breath in.
Again. In, two, three, four.
And slowly out, two, three, four, five, six.
Now, look around, and name to yourself a few things you can see.
Notice one thing you can hear, and one thing you can feel, the chair, your clothes, the air.
This is you, coming back into the present, out of the spinning thoughts.
Whatever brought you here, it is understandable, and you are not failing.
Place a hand on your chest if you like, and feel it rise, and fall.
Speak to yourself gently. This is hard, and I am doing my best.
Let the breath be long, and let the body begin to settle.
You are safe enough, right now, {name}. This will pass.
Stay with the slow breath, as long as you need.
